paragraphs: For ages, God's been trying to get in touch with our great-great-grandparents, using prophets and stuff. But now, He's talking to us straight up, through His Son. This is the guy who was there when God made everything, and one day, he's gonna inherit it all. He's like the spitting image of God, a total transformation of God's own awesomeness. And get this, he keeps the whole universe from falling apart just by talking. Talk about flexing his power.
§The Son Is Higher than Angels

So after he dealt with everyone's misfits, the Son got the ultimate promotion. He's now sitting in his honored place high in the heavens, right alongside God, way above any angel. I mean, did God ever say to an angel, "You're my boy, I'm so proud of you"? Nah. When he brings out his Son, it's like a world premiere, and he tells all the angels, "You better bow down to him."
When it comes to angels, God's like, 'Yeah, they're like super-fast messengers, like gusts of wind or flashes of fire.'

But to his Son, he says, 'You're God, and you're in charge forever. You're all about doing the right thing and you can't stand fakes. That's why I, your God, picked you to be the king and hooked you up with more good stuff than all your friends.'

And he's not done. He also says to the Son, "You're the one who kicked everything off, who built the earth and hung the stars. The earth and sky will get old and fall apart like a worn-out hoodie, and you'll just fold them up and put them away. But you? You'll never get old. You'll be the same, year after year, forever fresh."
And for the record, God never said to an angel, 'Come chill with me on my throne until I make your enemies your footstool.'
It's pretty clear that angels are just the support crew, sent to help out everyone who's getting saved.

title: Why Jesus is the GOAT
changes: Ch2: badges corrected to MSG (1-4 / 5-9 / 10-13 / 14-15 / 16-18)
Ch2: removed EN-added §Don't Drift Away (MSG has no header before 2:1-4); added MSG own header §The Salvation Pioneer (badged 5-9)
Ch2: split EN merged 15-18 para into MSG's 14-15 (flesh and blood, devil's hold on death) and 16-18 (for Abraham's crew, high priest) paras
Ch2: removed KO-only headers §흘러가지 말라 / "구원의 개척자이신 예수" / "다음 말씀도 자신을 그들과 한 가족으로 여기신다는 뜻임" / "또 이렇게도 말씀하셨음"; consolidated KO verse-level paras into MSG 5-9 and 10-13 paras 1:1 with EN
paragraphs: Alright, so listen up. You gotta pay attention to what we've learned, or you'll just drift off and forget it all. Back in the day, the message from the angels was the real deal, and if you messed up, you got called out. No exceptions. So, do you really think we can afford to sleep on this new message, this epic salvation? This isn't some hand-me-down story; the Master, Jesus himself, told us this stuff directly. And the people who heard him passed it on to us, so you know it's legit. Plus, God was dropping all sorts of signs and miracles, and the Holy Spirit was handing out gifts like it was nothing. He was basically flexing to show everyone this was the real deal.
§The Salvation Pioneer

Now, God didn't put angels in charge of the world to come, the one we're talking about. Someone in the Scriptures even asked, "Who are we that you even care about us? Why do you give us a second thought?" You made us a little lower than the angels, but you gave us a miraculous transformation and put us in charge of everything you made. But let's be real, we don't see ourselves running the whole show just yet. What we do see is Jesus. He was made a little lower than the angels for a bit, but after he faced death, he got the ultimate promotion. He's now crowned with more glory and honor than any angel. He basically took one for the team and died for every single one of us.

It totally makes sense that God, who started everything and keeps it all going, would make Jesus, our team captain for salvation, perfect by having him go through some tough stuff. He's leading us all to glory, after all. Since the one who saves us and those of us being saved are all from the same family, Jesus isn't embarrassed to call us his brothers and sisters. He even says, "I'm gonna tell my crew all about you, and we'll all praise you together." He's basically saying, "I'm on your team, I trust God just like you," and "Here I am with the squad God gave me."

Since we're all just regular people, it made sense for Jesus to become one of us. He did it to save us by dying himself. By facing death head-on, he totally wrecked the devil's power over it. He freed everyone who was basically living in fear of dying.

It's pretty clear he didn't do all this for the angels. He did it for us, for Abraham's crew. That's why he had to go through everything we go through. So when he stands before God as our High Priest to wipe our sins clean, he knows exactly what it feels like. He's been through the pain and the struggles, so he's the perfect one to help us when we need it.

title: Jesus vs. Moses: The Ultimate Showdown

splits.note: MSG 1-6 and 6-11 overlap on v6; badges kept as printed in MSG

Ch3: consolidated KO: single §우리 믿음의 중심 header (badged 1-6), merged 6-7+7-11 into 6-11, merged echo 15 into 12-14 per MSG layout
paragraphs: §The Centerpiece of All We Believe

Alright, listen up, my guys. If you're on this journey to be a better person, you gotta check out Jesus. Seriously. He's the real MVP, the main character of our whole faith. God gave him a job, and he totally crushed it. Yeah, Moses was a solid guy, super loyal. But Jesus? He's on a whole other level. He gets way more props. Think about it: the guy who builds the house is always gonna be more important than the house itself, right? Well, every house has a builder, but God is the OG builder of everything. Moses was like a good manager, keeping things in order and prepping for the main event. But Jesus is the owner's son, the one who's actually in charge of the whole place.

And here's the thing—if we stay confident and don't bail, we're part of that house too! That's why the Holy Spirit drops this truth bomb: "Hey, listen up today! Don't be like your ancestors who threw a fit and tested me in the desert. Even after watching me flex my power for forty years, they still wouldn't trust me. They kept trying to do their own thing, and it drove me nuts. I was so furious, I said, 'They're never gonna get it, they just refuse to follow my lead.' I was so done with them, I swore they'd never get to the promised land, never find their chill."

So, for real, watch your backs, fam. Don't let any sneaky doubts sneak in and make you ghost the living God. As long as it's 'today,' you gotta keep each other hyped and accountable, so sin doesn't make you lazy. If we just hang on to the awesome faith we started with, we're on Team Jesus for the long run. That message just keeps echoing, right? "Hey, listen up today! Don't be like your ancestors who threw a fit."

And who were those people who heard God and still ghosted him? Weren't they the same crew Moses led out of Egypt? And who did God have beef with for forty years? It was the ones who wouldn't listen and ended up as skeletons in the desert. And when God made that promise that they'd never make it, who was he talking to? The ones who wouldn't listen. They totally failed because they just wouldn't believe.

title: Don't Miss the Ultimate Chill Sesh

Ch4: removed KO-only lines §안식일의 쉼 / "믿음으로 약속을 받아들일 때"
paragraphs: §When the Promises Are Mixed with Faith

Alright, so check it. God’s promise to let us enter his ultimate chill zone is still on the table, so we gotta be super careful not to get disqualified. The Israelites back in the day got the same invite, but it was a total bust for them because they didn’t actually believe it. It was like getting a special access but then refusing to go inside. But for us, if we have faith, we get to experience that awesome rest. God was pretty furious with the others, saying, "They’ll never get to where they’re going, never be able to just sit down and chill."

God said that even though His part of the work was done since, like, the beginning of the world. You know how it says, "God rested on the seventh day after finishing his work"? But then He also says about the others, "They’ll never get to chill." So, the offer is still open. Those first guys totally missed out because they were stubborn and disobedient. God keeps hitting refresh on the promise, making "today" the day to get in on it, just like he said way later with King David: "Today, if you hear his voice, don’t be a blockhead."

So yeah, this promise is still live. It wasn’t a one-time thing with Joshua and his crew, otherwise God wouldn’t keep bringing it up. The promise of finally arriving and getting to rest is still there for God’s crew. God Himself is chilling, and when we finish our race, we’ll get to chill with Him. So let’s go hard and make sure we get to that place of rest, and not drop the ball by being disobedient.

God’s Word is no joke. What He says, goes. It’s like a super-sharp surgeon’s knife that cuts through all our excuses and doubts, laying everything bare. You can’t hide anything from Him; His Word sees right through you. It’s a total truth bomb, and you can’t escape it.
§The High Priest Who Cried Out in Pain

And the best part? We’ve got Jesus, our awesome High Priest with ready access to God. So let’s not let this opportunity slip. He’s not some out-of-touch leader; He gets what we’re going through. He’s faced all the same struggles and tests we do, but He never messed up. So we can walk right up to God with confidence and get the mercy and help we need, because He’s totally ready to give it. Just take it.

title: The Real High Priest
changes: Ch5: badges already match MSG (1-3 / 4-6 / 7-10 / 11-14)
Ch5: removed EN-added §Jesus the Great High Priest (MSG has no header before 5:1-3); added MSG own header §Re-Crucifying Jesus (badged 11-14)
Ch5: replaced KO-only headers §위대한 대제사장 예수님 / "그리스도 안에서 쑥쑥 자라가자" with §예수님을 다시 십자가에 못 박다 (badged 11-14)
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. Every head priest, picked to rep people in front of God and handle the sacrifices for when they mess up, has to be chill with everyone's slip-ups. Why? Because he's been there, done that, and gets it. But that also means he's gotta offer up sacrifices for his own blunders, not just for everyone else.

And get this: you don't just decide to be the head priest. God calls you, like he did with Aaron back in the day. Jesus didn't just promote himself to the top spot either. He was chosen by God, who was like, "You're my Son, and today we're celebrating you!" And another time, God said, "You're a priest forever, just like that mysterious guy Melchizedek."

When Jesus was on Earth, knowing he was going to die, he got real with God. He cried, he was in pain, and he prayed like a priest. And because he was straight-up with God, God heard him. Even though he was God's actual Son, he had to learn what it means to trust and obey by going through some rough stuff, just like we do. After he went through all that and basically leveled up to full maturity, God announced him as the new high priest, in the same league as Melchizedek. Now, he's the one who gives eternal life to everyone who listens and follows him.
§Re-Crucifying Jesus

Man, I've got so much more to say about this, but it's like talking to a wall. You guys have gotten into this gnarly habit of not even listening. By now, you should be the ones teaching this stuff, but instead, I've gotta go back to the baby steps with you, like you're learning about God for the first time. You're still on milk when you should be eating solid food! Milk is for newbies who don't get God's ways. The real food is for the pros who've had some practice and can tell what's right and what's wrong.

title: Level Up or Get Wrecked

paragraphs: Alright, let's get real. It's time to graduate from spiritual kindergarten. We've learned the basics: ditching the idea that we can save ourselves, trusting God, getting baptized, all that stuff. That's the foundation, but we can't just chill there. It's time to build something epic on it, you know? Time for a miraculous transformation in our faith.

Think about it. Some people get a taste of God's awesomeness, they see his power, they're part of the Holy Spirit's crew, and they experience how good God's Word is. But then they just ghost him. They walk away like it was nothing. That's a huge L. You can't just hit the reset button on that. It's like they're putting Jesus back on the cross and dissing him in front of everyone. Super messed up. It's like a field that gets plenty of rain. If it grows a bunch of awesome crops, the gardener is stoked. But if it just pops up a bunch of weeds, it's getting torched. No harvest, just a big ol' bonfire. You don't want to be that field.

But yo, I know you guys aren't like that. I've seen how you've shown love to God by helping out other Christians. That's legit. God sees that. So keep that same energy. Go all in on the hope you have, and don't get lazy. Be like the legends who kept the faith and got everything God promised them.
§God Gave His Word

When God made a promise to Abraham, he didn't mess around. He put his own name on the line, saying, "I'm gonna bless you like crazy—bless and bless and bless!" And Abraham was patient and got everything God promised. When we make promises, we might say "I swear on my mom's life" or something to show we're serious. God did the same thing, but he swore on himself because there's no one bigger. And God can't lie. His word is solid.

So for us, who are running to God for safety, we can grab onto that hope and never let go. It's like a spiritual lifeline that goes past all appearances right into the very presence of God, where Jesus, running on ahead of us, has taken up his permanent post as our High Priest in the order of Melchizedek.

title: The OG Priest Who's a Bigger Deal Than Abraham
changes: Ch7: replaced EN-added §Melchizedek with MSG own header §Melchizedek, Priest of God (badged 1-3)
Ch7: added MSG own header §A Permanent Priesthood (badged 11-14) in EN and KO
Ch7: replaced KO-only headers §멜기세덱 / §영원한 제사장이신 예수 with §하나님의 제사장, 멜기세덱 (1-3) and §영원한 제사장직 (11-14)
paragraphs: §Melchizedek, Priest of God

Alright, so check it. There's this guy, Melchizedek. He was the king of a place called Salem and a top-tier priest for the Most High God. After Abraham totally wrecked shop in a big battle, Melchizedek meets up with him and gives him a blessing. Abe, being the stand-up guy he is, gives Melchizedek a tenth of all the loot. Fun fact: 'Melchizedek' means 'King of Doing Right,' and 'Salem' means 'Peace,' so he's also the 'King of Peace.' This guy is like a legend from way back, no family tree on record, no beginning, no end. He's basically a mirror image of the Son of God, this epic priestly figure who's always been there.

You can tell Melchizedek was a big deal because even Father Abraham, the guy who started it all, gave him a ten percent cut of his winnings. Think about it: the priests from Levi's tribe, who are all related to Abraham, have a rule to collect a tenth from their own people. But this Melchizedek guy, a total outsider, collects it from Abraham and even blesses him—the guy who got all the promises from God! And everyone knows, when someone gives a blessing, the one giving it is the greater one.

Here’s another way to look at it: we give our money to priests who eventually die. But Abraham gave his to a priest who the Bible says 'lives.' You could even say that Levi, the ancestor of all the priests, basically paid his dues to Melchizedek through Abraham. It's like Melchizedek got the credit in the end.
§A Permanent Priesthood

The old system with the priests from Levi and Aaron's line was supposed to be the framework for God's law, but it couldn't actually make people perfect. If it had worked, there would've been no need to talk about a new kind of priest, one like Melchizedek. Since the old way didn't get the job done, the priesthood had to get a major update, which also meant the rules had to change. You can't explain Jesus using the old priest system, which is why he doesn't have any of them in his family background.

But the story of Melchizedek is the perfect setup. Jesus is a priest just like him, not because of who his ancestors were, but because of the raw power of his resurrection life. He's alive for good! The Bible even says he's a 'priest forever in the royal order of Melchizedek.' The old way of doing things, with all its rules that never really worked, got tossed aside. The law never led to a real transformation for anyone. But the new way—Jesus!—totally works. It gives us a direct line right into God's presence.

And here's the thing: the old priesthood was just passed down from father to son, no big ceremony or promise from God. But God stepped in and created this new, permanent priesthood with a solid promise: 'God gave his word; he won’t take it back: “You’re the permanent priest.”' This makes Jesus the guarantee of a way better deal between us and God—one that actually works. A whole new covenant.

Back in the day, there had to be a ton of priests, because they kept dying and needing to be replaced. But Jesus's priesthood is for keeps. He's on the job from now to eternity, ready to save everyone who comes to God through him. He's always there, speaking up for them like the ultimate wingman.

So now we have the perfect high priest for our needs. He's completely holy, never messed up by sin, and has authority that goes all the way up to God's throne room in heaven. Unlike the other high priests, he doesn't have to offer sacrifices for his own mistakes every day before he can even start helping us with ours. He did it once and for all when he offered up *himself* as the sacrifice. The old law made regular guys who could never get it right into high priests. But God's new command, which came later, appointed the Son, who is absolutely, eternally perfect. Mic drop.

title: God's New Game Plan
changes: Ch8: badges corrected to MSG (1-2 / 3-5 / 6-13)
Ch8: replaced EN-added §The New Covenant with MSG own header §A New Plan with Israel (badged 1-2)
Ch8: merged EN split 6-10 + 13 paras into single MSG 6-13 para (new covenant poem + old plan on the shelf)
Ch8: replaced KO-only headers §새 언약 / "새로운 약속" with §이스라엘과의 새 계획 (badged 1-2); merged KO 7-8+8-9+10-12+13 into single 6-13 para
paragraphs: §A New Plan with Israel

So, here's the deal. We've got this awesome High Priest, Jesus, who's like God's right-hand man. He's the one in charge of worship in the one true holy place, the one God himself built, not some copy.

The main job of a high priest is to offer gifts and sacrifices, and it's the same for Jesus. But if he were just stuck on Earth, he wouldn't even be a priest. We've already got plenty of those following the old rules. Those priests are just giving us a little preview of what's really going on in heaven. It's like when Moses got a quick look at the real thing before he built the tent for worship. God told him, "Hey, make sure you build it exactly like what I showed you on the mountain."

But Jesus's job as a priest is way better than theirs because he's working with a much better plan. If the first plan, the old agreement, had been perfect, we wouldn't have needed a new one. But it had some problems. God said, "Listen up! The time is coming when I'm going to make a new plan with my people. I'm getting rid of the old plan I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. They didn't stick to their part of the deal, so I had to let them go. This new plan I'm making isn't going to be written on paper or carved in stone. This time, I'm writing it directly in their hearts. I'll be their God, and they'll be my people. They won't have to go to school to learn about me or read a book to get it. Everyone will know me, from the least to the greatest. They'll know me because I'll forgive them, and I'll completely wipe their sins away." By creating a new plan, a new agreement between him and his people, God made the old one obsolete. It's like an old, dusty video game sitting on the shelf that no one plays anymore.

title: The Ultimate Holy Access
changes: Ch9: replaced EN-added §The Heavenly Tabernacle with MSG own header §A Visible Parable (badged 1-5)
Ch9: added MSG own header §Pointing to the Realities of Heaven (badged 11-15) in EN and KO

Ch9: replaced KO-only headers §하늘의 성막 / "§눈에 보이는 비유, 성소" with §눈에 보이는 비유 (badged 1-5)
paragraphs: §A Visible Parable

Alright, so check it. The first deal God had with his people had a whole bunch of rules for how to worship and a special place to do it. They set up this big tent, and in the main room, they had a lamp, a table, and some special bread. They called it the "Holy Place." But then there was another, even more exclusive room behind a curtain, called the "Holy of Holies." Inside, they had a gold altar for incense, and the Ark of the Covenant, which was covered in gold and held some crazy important stuff: a gold jar of manna (that magic bread from the desert), Aaron's staff that grew leaves, and the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments. And on top of the Ark were these awesome angel-wing statues. It was a pretty legit setup. We don't have time to get into all the details right now, though.

So, the regular priests would go into the main tent to do their jobs, but only the head priest could go into the inner room, the Holy of Holies, and only once a year. And when he did, he had to bring a blood sacrifice to cover his own mistakes and all the stuff the people had messed up. The Holy Spirit was basically showing them that as long as this old system was in place, nobody could just walk up to God. It was like a beta test. The gifts and sacrifices they offered couldn't really fix what was wrong on the inside or make people feel truly clean. It was all just a temporary fix until the real upgrade came along.
§Pointing to the Realities of Heaven

And then, BAM! The Messiah shows up. He's the high priest of a whole new, way better deal. He didn't bother with the old tent and all its props. He went straight into the real Holy Place in heaven, once and for all. And instead of sacrificing goats and calves, he used his own blood to set us free forever. If the old way of doing things could clean people up on the outside, imagine how much more powerful the blood of Christ is! He offered himself as the perfect sacrifice, a total transformation for our lives, inside and out. Now we're free from all that dead-end stuff of trying to be good enough on our own, and we can go all-in for God.

It's like this: when someone writes a will, it doesn't mean anything until they die. Jesus' death was what kicked the new deal into gear. His death was the moment everything switched from the old plan to the new one. It canceled out all the old debts and mistakes and let everyone who was promised a part of the inheritance finally get it. He brought God and people together in a totally new way.

Even the first deal needed a death to get it started. After Moses read all the rules of the old plan, he took the blood of sacrificed animals and sprinkled it on the rulebook and on the people. He was basically saying, "This is the blood that seals the deal God has made with you." He did the same thing with the special tent and everything in it. Pretty much everything in the old system depended on a death. That's why blood is such a big deal in the Bible, especially when it comes to forgiveness.

All that stuff with the blood and the sacrifices was just a picture of the real thing in heaven. That's why when the real thing happened, they didn't need all those animal sacrifices anymore. Jesus didn't go into a man-made copy of the Holy Place; he went into the real deal in heaven and offered himself as the one and only sacrifice for our sins. He didn't have to do it every year like the old priests did with animal blood. If that were the case, he would have had to die over and over again throughout history. But instead, he did it once and for all, a final mic drop that took care of sin forever.

Everyone has to die once, and then it's time to face the music. But Christ's death was a one-time sacrifice that wiped the slate clean for good. So when he shows up again, it won't be to deal with sin. It'll be to bring the ultimate prize: salvation for everyone who's been waiting for him.

title: Jesus Dropped the Mic

paragraphs: §The Sacrifice of Jesus

Alright, so check it. The old way of doing things, with all the rules and sacrifices? That was just a sneak peek, like a movie trailer for the awesome new plan. That old system was incomplete, a beta version, so it could never truly fix people. No matter how many animals they sacrificed, year after year, it was like trying to fill a bucket with a hole in it. It just reminded them of their mess-ups and made them feel even guiltier. Let’s be real, the blood of bulls and goats can’t just delete sin. It’s like trying to erase a permanent marker with a pencil eraser. Pointless.

This is what the prophecy was talking about, with Jesus saying: “You don’t want all these endless sacrifices. You gave me a body to be the real sacrifice. You’re not impressed by the smoke and smells from the altar. So I said, ‘I’m here to do it your way, God, just like it says in your book.’”

When Jesus said He was here to do it God’s way, He was basically saying the old plan was canceled. He came to roll out the new, perfect plan. And by sacrificing himself once and for all, he made us right with God. Total transformation.

Think about it: every other priest is on a hamster wheel, doing the same sacrifices every single day, year after year, and it never actually solves the sin problem. But Jesus, our High Priest, made one single sacrifice for all our sins, and then He sat down next to God, like a boss. Now He’s just waiting for his enemies to admit defeat. It was the perfect sacrifice from a perfect person to make us, a bunch of imperfect people, perfect in God’s eyes. With that one move, he did everything that needed to be done for anyone who wants to be made clean.

The Holy Spirit even confirms this, saying the new deal God is making with us won’t be written on paper or carved in stone. This time, God’s writing his plan *inside* us, on our hearts. And then He says, “I’ll completely forget their sins.” Once our sins are gone for good, there’s no need for any more sacrifices. Mic drop.
§Don't Throw It All Away

So, my guys, because of Jesus’ sacrifice, we can walk right up to God, into the Holy Place, with no hesitation. Jesus cleared the way for us. The curtain that used to block us from God’s presence? That’s Jesus’ body.

So let’s do it! Let’s go to God with total confidence, knowing we’re clean inside and out. Let’s hold on tight to the promises that keep us going, because God always keeps His word. Let’s get creative in how we show love and help each other out. Don’t be like those people who ghost worship services. Instead, let’s hype each other up, especially since we know the big day is coming.

If we bail on everything we’ve learned and been given, if we turn our backs on the truth, we’re basically spitting on Jesus’ sacrifice. Then we’re on our own, and we’ll have to face God’s judgment, which is going to be intense. If breaking the old rules meant you could be put to death, what do you think will happen if you diss God’s Son, disrespect the sacrifice that made you whole, and insult the Holy Spirit? This is not a small thing. God said He’ll get his vengeance and that He’ll judge his people. Nobody’s getting away with anything.

Remember when you first got it? Those were tough times. You were made fun of, people came at you from all sides. Sometimes it was you, sometimes it was your friends. If your friends went to jail, you had their backs. If your enemies came and took your stuff, you let it go with a smile, because you knew they couldn’t touch your real treasure. You were solid. So don’t throw it all away now. You were so sure of yourselves then, and you can still be sure now. You just have to stick with it and follow God’s plan. Then you’ll get the reward He promised. It won’t be long now. He’s on his way and will be here any minute. The people who are right with God live by their loyal trust in Him. If they cut and run, He won’t be happy. But we’re not quitters who are going to lose out. No way. We’re going to stick with it, trust God all the way, and we’re going to make it.

paragraphs: §Faith in What We Don't See

So, what's the deal with faith? It's basically being 100% sure about stuff you can't even see. It's the solid ground under everything that makes life awesome. This is what made our ancestors total legends.
By faith, we get that God created the entire universe with just a word. He made everything we see out of stuff we can't see. Mind-blowing, right?

Abel, because he had faith, gave God a way better offering than his brother Cain. It wasn't about the gift itself, but the fact that he believed. That's what got him on God's good side. And even now, we're still talking about it.

Then there's Enoch. This guy had so much faith he literally just vanished—God took him. Before he bounced, everyone knew he pleased God. You can't impress God without faith. Why? Because if you want to get close to God, you have to believe he's real and that he'll actually listen to you.

Noah's another one. God warned him about a flood when there wasn't a cloud in the sky, so what did he do? He built a massive boat in his backyard. Total leap of faith. And because he did, his family was saved. His faith totally roasted the rest of the world and showed everyone what's up. That's how Noah and God became best buds.

And don't even get me started on Abraham. God told him to pack his bags and move to a place he'd never even heard of, and he just did it. No questions asked. He lived in tents like a nomad, and so did his son Isaac and his grandson Jacob, all because they were holding on to the same promise. Abraham was waiting for a real city, one designed and built by God himself.

Sarah, Abraham's wife, was way too old to have kids, but because she had faith, she got pregnant. She knew the One who made the promise would keep it. And from this one old guy, a whole nation was born, more people than you can count.

All these heroes of faith died before they got what was promised, but they saw it coming from a distance and were cool with it. They knew they were just visitors here on Earth. They were looking for a better place—heaven. That's why God is so proud of them and has a city waiting for them.

Remember when God tested Abraham and told him to sacrifice his son, Isaac? The son God had promised him? Abraham was ready to do it, because he figured God could just bring Isaac back from the dead if he wanted to. And in a way, that's what happened.
Isaac, with faith, blessed his sons Jacob and Esau for the future.
Jacob, on his deathbed, blessed each of Joseph's sons.
And Joseph, as he was dying, told everyone that Israel would leave Egypt and even planned his own burial.
Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born because they saw he was a special kid and weren't scared of the king's orders.

When Moses grew up, he refused to be called a prince of Egypt. He chose to suffer with God's people rather than live a cushy life of sin. He knew that sticking with the Messiah was worth more than all the treasure in Egypt. He wasn't scared of the king's rage because he kept his eyes on the God no one can see. And by faith, he kept the Passover Feast and sprinkled the Passover blood on each house, so the destroyer of the firstborn wouldn't touch them.
By faith, the Israelites walked right through the Red Sea on dry land. The Egyptians tried to follow and got totally wiped out.
By faith, the Israelites marched around Jericho for seven days and the walls just fell down.
And Rahab, a prostitute in Jericho, had faith and welcomed the spies, so she was saved when everyone else who didn't trust God was destroyed.

I could go on all day about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and all the prophets. These guys were the ultimate faith all-stars. They took down kingdoms, made things right, and got what God promised them. They shut the mouths of lions, walked through fire, and survived getting stabbed. They turned their weaknesses into strengths, won battles, and sent entire armies running. Women even got their dead loved ones back. Some were tortured but refused to give in because they were waiting for something better: a transformation to a new life. Others were made fun of, whipped, thrown in jail, stoned, and sawed in two. They were homeless and had to wear animal skins, but the world wasn't even worthy of them.

None of these people, even with their amazing faith, got everything that was promised. God had a better plan for us. He wanted their story and our story to come together to make one epic saga. Their journey of faith isn't complete without ours.

paragraphs: §Discipline in a Long-Distance Race

Hey, check it out. You're surrounded by a massive crowd of faith legends, all of them cheering you on from the sidelines. It's like you're in the championship game, and all the greats who played before you are screaming your name. So, what's the move? You gotta get in the zone! Drop all the extra baggage, the bad habits and secret sins that are just weighing you down and making you trip. It's time to run your race, and don't even think about quitting.

Keep your eyes locked on the ultimate coach, Jesus. He invented this race, and he's the one who crossed the finish line to show us how it's done. Just think about his gameplay. He never lost focus on the epic win waiting for him—that awesome victory party with God. That's why he could handle all the crazy stuff they threw at him: the cross, people totally dissing him, you name it. And now? He's chilling in the place of honor, right next to God. So, whenever you feel like your faith is running on low battery and you're about to give up, just replay his highlight reel. Remember all the haters and the tough times he pushed through. That'll give you the adrenaline shot you need to get back in the game.

And for real, in this battle against sin, you haven't even come close to what others have gone through, let alone the ultimate sacrifice Jesus made. So, no feeling sorry for yourself. Think of it like this: God is your dad, and he's training you. When you get disciplined, don't just shrug it off, but don't get totally crushed by it either. It's because he loves you that he corrects you. This isn't a punishment; it's a training montage to make you stronger. It might be rough at the moment, but later on, you'll see the payoff. You'll be spiritually jacked and have a solid connection with God.
So, no more slacking! Get up, get moving, and clear the path for the long-distance runners — help your friends out so nobody gets left behind or twists an ankle. And run for it!

Make it your mission to get along with everyone and to stay tight with God. If you don't, you'll miss out on seeing him in action. Don't let anyone in your crew miss out on God's awesome generosity. Keep an eye out for any negativity or bitterness. That stuff spreads like weeds and can wreck the whole squad. And whatever you do, don't pull an Esau. That guy traded away a lifetime of blessings for a quick snack. You know how he totally regretted it later and cried his eyes out, but it was too late. Don't trade your future glory for a moment of instant gratification.
§An Unshakable Kingdom
Remember, you're not dealing with the old-school, scary version of meeting God — like your ancestors at that terrifying, fiery mountain.

Nah, you've got an invite to something way better. You've come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God. It's a massive party with tons of angels and all the other followers of Christ. You've come to Jesus, the guy who hooked us up with a brand-new deal with God. His death wasn't a call for revenge; it was a shout-out of pure grace.

So, listen up. If the people way back when got in huge trouble for ignoring the earthly warnings, imagine what will happen if we ghost the warnings from heaven. God's voice once stunned the ground, but next time, he's going to rock the heavens too. He's doing a total house-cleaning to get rid of all the temporary junk, so only the real, unshakable stuff remains.

Do you get what you're a part of? An unshakable kingdom! That should make you incredibly thankful. So let's worship God with everything we've got, showing him major respect. Because our God isn't just some spectator in the stands. He's in the game, and he's a consuming fire, burning away everything that's not pure. He's on a mission to cleanse everything, and he won't stop until the job is done.

paragraphs: §Jesus Doesn't Change

Alright, let's wrap this up. Keep it real with each other, always showing love. Don't be stingy; share your food and your space. You never know, you might be chilling with angels and not even know it! And for those in jail or getting a raw deal, feel for them like it's happening to you. Marriage is a big deal, so treat it like one. God's not cool with people messing around.
Don't get obsessed with stuff. Be cool with what you've got. God's got your back and will never ghost you. So you can say, "God's on my team, I'm not scared. What can anyone do to me?"

Don't forget the leaders who taught you about God. Check out how they live their lives and learn from them. They're the real deal, and so is Jesus. He's the same yesterday, today, and forever. Seriously.
Don't get sidetracked by weird new ideas about God. His grace is all you need. All that other stuff is just noise. Those knockoff 'Christian' products don't do much for anyone who buys them.

The altar where God gives us the gift of himself isn't some buffet for insiders to grab and loot. In the old system, the animals were killed and their bodies disposed of outside the camp, while the blood was brought inside to the altar as a sacrifice for sin. It's the same with Jesus — he was crucified outside the city gates, and that's where he poured out the sacrificial blood that was brought to God's altar to cleanse his people.

So let's go outside, where Jesus is, where the action is — not trying to be privileged insiders, but taking our share of the heat along with Jesus. This insider world isn't our home; we've got our eyes peeled for the City that's coming. Let's take our place outside with Jesus, pouring out sacrificial praises from our lips to God in Jesus' name instead of animal blood.

And don't slack on working for the common good — keep doing good stuff and sharing what you have. God takes particular pleasure in that kind of 'sacrifice,' the kind that happens in the kitchen, at work, and on the streets.
Listen to your leaders. They're looking out for you and have to answer to God. Make their job a joy, not a pain. Why would you want to make things harder for them?
Pray for us. We're trying to do the right thing, but it's tough. We need your prayers to get back to you soon.

May the God of peace, who brought back Jesus our Great Shepherd from the dead through the blood sacrifice that sealed the eternal covenant, hook you up with everything you need to please him. May he work in us what gives him most pleasure, through Jesus the Messiah. All glory to Jesus forever and always! Oh, yes, yes, yes.
P.S. I kept this short and sweet, so take it seriously. Good news! Timothy's out of jail. If he's quick, I'll bring him with me when I visit.
Say hi to all your leaders and everyone else. The crew from Italy says 'sup.
Grace be with you all.
